text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's President Zhelyu Zhelev discussed with Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov and Bulgarian National Bank governor Lyubomir Philipov the amendments in the Deposit Guarantee Law that was voted in parliament last week.
-- Serbian customs officers seized 190 kg of heroin worth some 200 million German marks at Bulgaria's border with former Yugoslavia in a truck with Slovenian registration.

-- The head of Bulgaria's Posts and Telecommunication Committee, Lyubomir Kolarov, said 25 percent of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company will be sold at an international public tender and the announcement for the tender will be published in the foreign press.

-- Bulgaria's Securities and Stock Exchange Committee said it has granted a licence for operation to five voucher privatisation funds. Eighty out of the 81 funds that raised the minimum required capital of 70 million levs had deposited requests for a licence by the October 7 deadline.

-- A South Korean company will probably extend a $10 million loan for the modernisation of Bulgaria's largest oil refinery Neftochim, the newspaper reported, without quoting sources. It did not name the company.

-- Bulgaria's largest private conglomerate Multigroup plans to set up a joint company with Russia's United Energy Systems. The new company will provide electricity in the Balkans and will be called Balkan Energy Systems, Multigroup's Vice President Nikolai Valkanov said.

-- Bulgaria, Greece and Russia are expected to discuss at a trilateral meeting in November a pipeline to carry gas and oil through Bulgaria's territory, the deputy chairman of Russia's parliament Michail Yuriev said after talks with Bulgaria's Prime Minister Zhan Videnov.

-- Bulgaria's central bank is expected to decide this month for which of the nine local commercial banks placed under special supervision last month to seek insolvency through courts, a banker said. Sequestrators' reports are due to be presented at the Central Bank by October 16.
